assessment.nobel_worthiness: A foundational, wide-ranging political-economy programme linking political institutions, state capacity, electoral incentives and fiscal policy.
assessment.attribution: The three named scholars represent central and complementary theoretical and empirical strands of this programme.
assessment.maturity: The work has shaped research and policy analysis over several decades and its implications remain highly active.
uncertainties: The contribution spans several connected literatures, making a single prize citation necessarily selective.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The work transformed understanding of how trade and technology shocks affect local labour markets, employment and inequality.
assessment.attribution: Autor, Dorn and Hanson have a particularly coherent joint contribution on exposure to trade shocks and labour-market adjustment.
assessment.maturity: Its findings have been extensively studied and have reshaped debates on trade policy and distribution.
uncertainties: Separating the effects of trade, technology and other regional changes remains empirically demanding.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Administrative-data research on intergenerational mobility has made inequality of opportunity measurable at unprecedented geographic and social scale.
assessment.attribution: Chetty and Hendren are central to the mobility atlas programme, with Katz contributing importantly to its connection with neighbourhood and social policy.
assessment.maturity: The data infrastructure and research findings have produced a mature, influential body of work.
uncertainties: Observed mobility patterns do not by themselves identify all causal mechanisms behind place effects.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: This research reconstructed long-run top-income and wealth distributions and brought tax records and offshore wealth to the centre of inequality analysis.
assessment.attribution: Piketty, Saez and Zucman form a clear intellectual grouping across historical measurement, taxation and hidden wealth.
assessment.maturity: The work has generated durable data resources, extensive follow-on research and major public-policy relevance.
uncertainties: Wealth capitalization, valuation and offshore-asset estimates remain sensitive to measurement assumptions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The misallocation framework gave a powerful quantitative account of how distorted input allocation can depress aggregate productivity and income.
assessment.attribution: Hsieh, Klenow and Restuccia are principal contributors to the development and application of this research programme.
assessment.maturity: It is a well-established framework with broad influence in development, growth and firm dynamics.
uncertainties: Measured dispersion can reflect adjustment costs, demand conditions and measurement error as well as distortions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Audit and correspondence designs made discrimination in labour markets directly testable and established a highly influential empirical approach.
assessment.attribution: Bertrand and Mullainathan made the seminal field-experimental contribution, while Charles has made major related contributions to the economics of racial inequality.
assessment.maturity: The methods have been replicated widely across countries and have enduring consequences for labour-market research.
uncertainties: Audit studies identify treatment at the application stage but do not capture every mechanism generating labour-market inequality.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The measurement and analysis of management practices established organizational quality as an important and tractable source of productivity differences.
assessment.attribution: Bloom, Van Reenen and Sadun are central to the international management-survey and organizational-capital research programme.
assessment.maturity: The research has accumulated evidence across firms and countries and has stimulated a large follow-on literature.
uncertainties: The causal effect of measured management practices remains difficult to fully disentangle from selection and complementary inputs.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Research on reciprocity, fairness and inequity aversion changed economic models of incentives, cooperation and institutions.
assessment.attribution: Fehr, Falk and Schmidt made closely linked experimental and theoretical contributions to the social-preferences literature.
assessment.maturity: The work is long established, extensively tested and influential across behavioural, labour and organizational economics.
uncertainties: The stability and external validity of measured social preferences can depend on institutional and experimental context.
